title: Meet the 26 letters
goal: Recognize the shapes. Get to know their names.

study.title: Small shapes. So many possibilities.
paragraphs: Written English uses 26 letters. Each has an uppercase form and a lowercase form. Together, they build names, messages, stories, and ideas.
The alphabet has a long history through earlier writing systems. You are learning a set of shared symbols, not 26 unrelated drawings.
Look at both forms. Some are similar, such as C and c. Others, such as A and a, look quite different. A letter’s name is not always the sound it represents in a word.

study.title: Meet the alphabet.
paragraphs: Choose a letter to hear its name using your device’s English voice. The voice can vary between devices.

study.title: Look, listen, and say it.
paragraphs: Take a few letters at a time. Look at the shape, listen to the name, and say it aloud. You can revisit a letter whenever you need.
Next, put those names into a familiar sequence with the alphabet song.
